speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to help you, I need to ask a few questions about your symptoms and history. Has your breathing been rapid, is there any grunting or flaring of the nostrils, and did the pregnancy or birth have any complications?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history; the preterm birth at 32 weeks, cesarean delivery, and maternal gestational diabetes are significant risk factors. Given the respiratory distress, have you noticed cyanosis (bluish skin) or retractions (skin pulling in around the ribs) when the baby breathes?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome

The history of 32-week gestation and maternal gestational diabetes strongly supports a diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) in a preterm infant. The response to oxygen administration is consistent with RDS rather than a urinary tract infection, which does not present with primary respiratory distress.
